limitations: Discovery is syntactic: no symbol table and no cross-unit type resolution (Stage 2).
No semantic intermediate representation is built (Stage 2).
Binary files (.exe, .dll, .bpl, .dcu, .ocx ...) are inventoried and hashed but never decompiled or executed.
No compiler is invoked and no build is attempted; the compiler named is inferred from file extensions, directives and project metadata.
Databases are never connected to; database technologies and SQL dialects are detected from source and SQL files only.
Dependency resolution is limited to the ingested input: a unit or library that is absent is reported as unresolved, not searched for.
Library, integration and runtime-dependency detection is heuristic (PARTIAL); a finding is evidence of a reference, not proof that the dependency is exercised at run time.
Evidence lists are capped at 25 entries per item and the structure tree at 50 files per group; the full file list is in inventory.csv.
Delphi ProjectVersion values are reported as stated; they are not mapped to a product release name.
GUI forms are detected and counted, not converted; GUI conversion is out of scope for the first release.
Nothing in this blueprint is VERIFIED: equivalence with a Java translation is only measurable from Stage 5.
